text: Do you think geography is boring?
Wait till you see these places,
because the world is full of places that make no sense.
Let's get started with our countdown
of the eight biggest geography lies that you believed.
Number eight, Mount Everest is the world's tallest mountain.
Let's start with the big one.
Everyone knows Mount Everest
is the tallest mountain on earth, right?
Wrong, this is probably the biggest lie in geography.
The real tallest mountain is Mauna Kea in Hawaii,
From base to peak it's 33,500 feet tall. That's 4,500 feet taller than Everest.
The only reason nobody talks about this is because most of Mauna Kea is underwater, so
technically you'd need scuba gear to climb the world's actual tallest mountain.
7. The Sahara Desert is Just Sand When people picture the Sahara, they see
endless sand dunes. But sand only covers about 25% of the Sahara. Most of it is actually
rocky plateaus, gravel plains and mountains. The sand dune image comes from movies and
postcards, but it's not what most of the Sahara actually looks like.
6. The Red Sea is Red
The Red Sea has red right in the name so the water must be red, right? The water is actually
blue like any other sea. The name comes from seasonal algae blooms that sometimes create
reddish patches, but 99% of the time it looks like normal blue ocean water.
5. Alaska is huge compared to other countries
Speaking of map lies, Alaska looks enormous on most maps, bigger than Brazil or Australia.
Australia. Brazil is 5 times bigger than Alaska, and Australia is 4 times bigger. The same
map distortion that makes Greenland look massive also makes Alaska look like a giant,
when it's actually much smaller than you think.
Number 4. The Caspian Sea is a sea, and it's salty like an ocean. But it's actually
the world's largest lake. It's completely surrounded by land, with no connection to
any ocean. We just call it a sea because it's so big and salty. But geographically,
It's a lake.
Number 3.
Rivers always flow north to south.
This seems logical because we think of north as up and south as down on maps, but rivers
flow downhill, and downhill can be in any direction.
The Nile flows north, the Mississippi flows south, the Amazon flows east.
Rivers don't care about your map directions, they just follow gravity.
Number two, Holland and the Netherlands are the same thing.
Millions of people think Holland is a country.
It's not.
Holland is just one region inside the Netherlands. Calling the whole country
Holland is like calling all of America Texas. Some Dutch people actually get
annoyed when you do this. So now you know better. Number one, Africa is mostly in
the southern hemisphere. Look at most maps and Africa seems like it's mostly
below the equator. Wrong again. Almost two-thirds of Africa is actually in the
northern hemisphere. Countries like Egypt, Libya, Algeria, and most of Nigeria are all
north of the equator. This is Boogal. Follow for more geography-fun facts!
